The source next specifies −H+. The theorem proves graph equality, valence, composition, zero charge, one radical, and no stereochemical annotations.

The subsequent −e− step converts the alpha-amino radical into the explicit iminium graph (HOCH2CH2)2N+=CH–CH2OH. The theorem checks the N=C double bond, N formal charge +1, C6H14NO3 composition, no radical, valid valence, and no applicable stereochemical annotation.

Hydrolysis under the printed +H2O/−H+ operation yields the explicit diethanolamine graph HN(CH2CH2OH)2. The theorem proves equality with derived6, C4H11NO2 composition, neutrality, valid valence, absence of radicals/stereochemical annotations, and absence of an aldehyde carbon.

The other hydrolysis fragment is the explicit glycolaldehyde graph HOCH2–CHO. This agrees with the source clue that species 7 gives a silver mirror. The theorem proves equality with derived7, C2H4O2 composition, neutrality, valid valence, absence of radicals/stereochemical annotations, and presence of a hydrogen-bearing carbon double-bonded to oxygen.
